name: Native Hawaiians (Kanaka Maoli flag, United States)
description: Nine horizontal stripes repeating green, red and yellow, charged at the centre with a green shield bearing a yellow kahili (feather standard) between two crossed paddles.
history: The Kanaka Maoli flag was popularised in 2001 by Gene Simeona, who presented it as a pre-1843 flag of the Hawaiian Kingdom; it is widely used by the Hawaiian sovereignty movement. The kahili stands for the aliʻi (chiefly class) and the paddles for the voyaging heritage.
